cards.text: This psalm opens with the writer talking to his own soul, then turning to speak to the LORD. He tells the LORD He is very great, clothed with splendor and majesty. And friend, he's just getting warmed up.

cards.question: The writer pictures the LORD dressed in splendor. What does the LORD wrap Himself in like a garment?

cards.text: He wears LIGHT, friend, and He stretches out the heavens like a tent, laying the beams of His chambers in the waters above. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer begging for one little slice of light, and He puts it on like a jacket.

cards.question: The writer pictures the LORD making the clouds His chariot and walking on the wings of the wind.
The writer says the LORD makes the winds His messengers and flames of fire His servants. So even the wildest forces ___ Him.

cards.text: Now the writer looks down at the earth, set on its foundations, never to be moved. That's steadier than anything I've ever stood on, and friend, I stand on GOLD.

cards.question: The writer says God covered the earth with the deep like a garment. How high did the waters stand?
When the LORD rebukes the waters covering the earth, they rise even higher.

cards.text: At the sound of His thunder, the waters hurry away. Hurrying off at one loud sound? Friend, that's me every time my oven timer goes off. I jump a foot in the air, base and all.
The mountains rise and the valleys sink, each one to the place God assigned for it. Every mountain right where He put it, and I can't find my own spatula.

cards.question: Then God sets a boundary the waters cannot cross. Why?

answers.text: So they never cover the earth again
So the ships can sail safely
So the fish stay in one place

cards.text: Next, God sends springs into the valleys, running right between the mountains. Fresh water flowing free, friend, and not one bill at the end of the month.

cards.question: The springs God sends into the valleys give drink to every beast of the field.

cards.text: The birds nest beside the springs and sing among the branches, and I bet not one of them ever hit snooze. God waters the mountains from His chambers, and the earth is satisfied by the fruit of His works.

cards.question: God makes the grass grow for the ___ and provides crops for people to cultivate.

cards.text: From the earth comes wine that gladdens the heart, oil that makes a face shine, and bread that sustains the heart. Not just enough to get by, friend, but gladness too.

cards.question: The cedars of Lebanon have their fill too. Who planted those cedars?

cards.text: Birds build their nests in those cedars, and the stork makes her home in the cypresses.
The high mountains are for the wild goats, and the cliffs are a refuge for the rock badgers. Ducking into the cliffs? That's me behind the cooling racks every time a batch comes out burnt.

cards.question: Trees, birds, storks, goats and rock badgers. What's the big picture the writer paints here?

answers.text: God gives each creature its place
Every creature must fight for space
People rule over the wild places

cards.text: Now the writer looks up: God made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun knows when to set. The SUN knows when to clock out, friend, and I've got a timer AND I still burn a batch.

cards.question: When God brings darkness and it becomes night, the beasts of the forest settle down to sleep.

cards.text: Night is when the beasts of the forest prowl, and the young lions roar for their prey. Friend, I spent years in a dark drawer, and the scariest thing in there was an expired coupon.

cards.question: The writer says those roaring young lions seek their food from God.
When the sun rises, the young lions withdraw and lie down in their ___.

cards.text: The lions clock out, and people clock in. Man goes out to his work and his labor until evening.
Then the writer says, "How many are Your works, O LORD!" Friend, I lose count of my cookie boxes before lunch.

cards.question: The writer says the earth is full of God's creatures. What did God make them all in?

cards.text: Then he points to the sea, vast and wide, teeming with creatures great and small. Ships sail through, and so does Leviathan, and friend, I'd be the one on deck yelling LOOK AT THE SIZE OF THAT THING.

cards.question: Out in that vast sea is Leviathan. What does the writer say God formed Leviathan to do there?
All of God's creatures look to Him to give them their ___ in due season.

cards.text: When God gives it, they gather it up, and when He opens His hand, they're satisfied with good things. Like a whole office the second somebody cracks open a cookie box in the break room.

cards.question: When God hides His face, the creatures are terrified. When He takes away their breath, what happens?

answers.text: They die and return to dust
They fall into a deep sleep
They wander off to the sea

cards.question: When God sends His Spirit, creatures are ___ and He renews the face of the earth.

cards.text: Then the writer says, "May the glory of the LORD endure forever; may the LORD rejoice in His works." And when the LORD looks on the earth, it trembles.

cards.question: The earth trembles when the LORD looks at it. What happens when He touches the mountains?
After looking at everything God made, the writer says he will sing to the LORD all his life.

cards.text: Then the writer says, "May my meditation be pleasing to Him, for I rejoice in the LORD." And he adds, "May sinners vanish from the earth and the wicked be no more."

cards.question: The writer ends by telling his soul to bless the LORD, the same call he opened with, then adds a Hallelujah. What does ending where he began show?

answers.text: His whole song is wrapped in praise
He is starting the song over again
He is turning to a new subject

findings.problem: The card retells the lions withdrawing at sunrise from Psalm 104:22 in "The lions clock out," then tells about people going to work from Psalm 104:23. It cites only Psalm 104:23, so its citation should be Psalm 104:22-23.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
